2147:
## In short

**Gaṅgādāsa**, a brāhmaṇa of **Anādi**, is named in the Vaiṣṇava-vandanās of **Jīva Gosvāmī**, **Devakīnandana** and **Vṛndāvana dāsa**.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Gaṅgā Dāsa» #291 until 07-11-2026.
2170:
## In short

**Navadvīpacandra dāsa** was a composer of padas; pada **2961** of the **Padakalpataru**, on nāma-saṅkīrtana, is his.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record of Navadvīpacandra dāsa, disciple of Rādhāramaṇa-caraṇa dāsa (#1020), until 11-11-2026.
707:
## In short

**Kavicandra**, son of **Kavi Karṇapūra** and a resident of **Khaṇḍaghoṣa**, translated the **Gīta-govinda** into Bengali verse.

## Sources

The record's text. Two other Kavicandras once in this record — the one of Lord Caitanya's branch and the one who taught Rasikānanda as a child (#2104) — have their own records.
1991:
## In short

**Gaṅgā-devī** was the mother of **Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi** and the wife of **Bāṇeśvara Brahmacārī** (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Gaṅgā Devī» 1).

## Sources

The record's notes and text. Not Gaṅgā-devī, Śrī Nityānanda's daughter.
2115:
## In short

**Kṛṣṇadāsa** wrote the Bengali poem **Govinda-maṅgala**, kept in the Pāṭabāḍī collection (Vaṅka 14).

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Others» #1888 until 07-11-2026.
2175:
## In short

**Rasikānanda**, a Vaiṣṇava poet, wrote pada **2227** of the **Padakalpataru**, on Lord Gaurāṅga's acceptance of sannyāsa. He may be Rasikānanda Prabhu (#1908); the text does not say.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record of Rasikamohana Vidyābhūṣaṇa (#1303) until 11-11-2026.
1949:
## In short

**Rāmadāsa** was the second son of **Śivānanda Sena** (#1427); in his former life he was **Vicakṣaṇa Śuka**, the parrot (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 145).

## Sources

The record's text.
1979:
## In short

**Haridāsa**, a padakartā, has six songs in the **Padakalpataru**; the finest is no. **3014**: «nācite nā jāni tabu nāciye gaurāṅga bali'» — «I do not know how to dance, yet I dance saying Gaurāṅga; I do not know how to sing, yet I sing» (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 4).

## Sources

The record's notes and text.
2107:
## In short

**Rasamaya dāsa** wrote the **Śrī Kṛṣṇa-bhakti-vallī** (Viśva-bhāratī manuscript no. 59, dated 1172 BS / 1765).

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Rasamaya Dāsa» #1299 until 07-11-2026.
2020:
## In short

**Gopāla dāsa** was one of the translators of the **Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka** of Rāmānanda Rāya (Calcutta University manuscript 2582, 1235 BS).

## Sources

The record's text (from «Vaiṣṇava Biographies A-Z»).
2131:
## In short

**Mādhava** was a composer of padas: there are **fifty-five** padas with the bhaṇitā «Mādhava» in the **Padakalpataru**.

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Mādhava» #867 until 07-11-2026.
1078:
## In short

**Paramānanda Vaidya** of Nadia was the paternal grandfather of **Śrī Jagadānanda**.

## Sources

The record's text («see Jagadānanda»; which Jagadānanda is not said).
1812:
## In short

**Bhakti Vistāra Viṣṇu**, an ācārya of the mission of Śrīla **Bhakti Vicāra Yāyāvara Mahārāja** (#1667), was a founding member of the **World Vaiṣṇava Association** (WVA).

## Sources

The record's text.
1981:
## In short

**Haridāsa** of **Orissa**, a devotee of Lord Gaurāṅga, wrote in the sixteenth century of the Śaka era the **Mayūra-candrikā**, whose twentieth candrikā is a hymn to Mahāprabhu (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Haridāsa» 2).

## Sources

The record's notes and text.
2104:
## In short

**Kavicandra** taught **Rasikānanda Prabhu** in his childhood (Rasikamaṅgala Pūrva 9.26).

## Sources

The record's text. It was in the record «Kavicandra» #707 until 07-11-2026.
